title: Progressive eval fence and signal debouncing for canary flips
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem:
Teams performing canary and A/B flips are seeing spiky, non-actionable eval failures because single-prompt regressions and short-lived noise cause unnecessary rollbacks or noisy alerts. Current gating is too brittle: it treats prompt-set aggregate deltas as instantaneous signals and lacks hysteresis, per-prompt noise models, and per-customer baselines.

Goal:
Build a progressive 'eval fence' that ties quality regression monitoring to curated reference prompt sets (customer- and workload-aware), debounces transient signals, and exposes explicit hysteresis policies to the rollout orchestrator so we only auto-halt or rollback on sustained, statistically significant regressions.

Scope and approach (high level):
1) Reference prompt set model: maintain 'reference' prompt collections (global and per-customer) with metadata: traffic-weight, intent, acceptance tolerance. These are the canonical evaluation probes used by the fence.
2) Signal processing pipeline: compute per-prompt metrics (score, token-likelihood flags, structural diffs) every rolling window (default 10 minutes). Produce both point estimates and uncertainty (moving variance) for each prompt.
3) Noise-tolerant gating rules: create a rule engine that supports:
   - adaptive thresholds: threshold = baseline_mean +/- k * baseline_std, derived from historical window for that prompt and customer segment;
   - consecutive-failure hysteresis: require N consecutive windows exceeding threshold before triggering a gate (default N=3);
   - fraction-of-prompts rule: allow gated action when X% of critical prompts fail for Y windows (default 25% over 3 windows) to catch multi-prompt regressions;
   - debouncing: back-off window grows on unstable signals to avoid flip-flopping;
   - severity tiers: warn -> quarantine -> halt -> full rollback; each tier has configurable timeouts and actions.
4) Integration with rollout orchestrator: fence exposes a small API (evaluateFence(canaryId)) returning {statusTier, triggers, suggestedAction}. Orchestrator consumes this and executes policy (scale-down, route-to-shadow, rollback).
5) Telemetry, dashboards, and alerting: surface per-prompt score distributions, drift heatmaps, trigger history, and confidence bands. Alerts should include runbook links and suggested mitigations.

Acceptance criteria:
- Eval fence ingests reference prompt sets and computes per-prompt rolling statistics with <5s end-to-end latency from eval result to fence decision.
- Hysteresis rules must prevent any single-window-triggered rollback in the canary simulation suite (see tests).
- Automated rollback is only executed after 'halt' tier returned for at least 3 consecutive windows or when fraction-of-prompts rule fires.
- Console exposes: (a) active fence status per rollout, (b) per-prompt time-series, (c) ability to mute a prompt for a rollout.
- Runbook added and QA validates behavior under three simulated noise profiles (spike, drift, bursty flapping).

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Adaptive thresholds increase robustness but can mask slow regressions; to mitigate, we compute both short-term and long-term baselines and expose drift alerts if long-term mean shifts steadily.
- Per-customer baselines improve sensitivity but require storage and warm-up — new deployments will start with global baselines and auto-initialize customer baselines after N samples.
- Conservative hysteresis reduces false positives at the cost of slower detection; we parametrize hysteresis so product teams can opt for more aggressive policies for critical releases.

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) Eval pipeline changes (2 sprints): add per-prompt variance and windowed aggregator, store historical baseline buckets.
2) Rule engine + API (1 sprint): implement adaptive thresholding, hysteresis, and tiered actions.
3) Orchestrator integration (1 sprint): wire evaluateFence into canary state machine; add simulator hooks.
4) Console + alerting (1 sprint): new UI panels, runbook links, mute controls.
5) QA + rollout (1 sprint): synthetic tests, staged rollout to pilot customers, iterate on defaults.

Telemetry and metrics to ship:
- fence_evaluations_total (by rollout, tier)
- fence_trigger_rate (per-prompt, per-customer)
- avg_windows_to_halt
- false_positive_rate (estimated in simulation)
- time_saved_by_debounce (tokens/requests avoided)

Acceptance test plan / simulation harness:
- Build a canary simulator that replays historical traffic with injected anomalies (single-prompt spike, coordinated multi-prompt drift, sustained low-amplitude regression). We must pass the no-rollback-on-spike test and trigger-on-sustained-drift test.

Operational runbook (short):
- On WARN: investigate per-prompt chart; if a known flake, mute the prompt for the rollout.
- On QUARANTINE: reduce canary weight to 5% and enable shadowing to capture more data.
- On HALT: stop rollout and trigger on-call paging; automatically spawn rollback job if HALT persists for configured timeout.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ML/Progressive+Eval+Fence (placeholder)
- Simulator repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/canary-simulator/pull/314 (placeholder)
- UX mockups: Drive -> /Shared/Console/FenceMockups (placeholder)

Open questions / future enhancements:
- Should we expose a CLI for customers to tune their per-customer thresholds? (ops security and audit implications)
- How fast should customer baselines adapt after model changes? (risk of masking model-wide regressions)
- Explore using bootstrapped confidence intervals vs Gaussian assumption for low-volume prompts.

Estimated work items (PR breakdown):
- eval/aggregator: implement rolling stats and baseline store (PR: redwood/runtime#xxxx)
- fence/service: rule engine and API (PR: redwood/services#xxxx)
- orchestrator: consume fence decisions and map to actions (PR: redwood/orch#xxxx)
- console: UI and alert integration (PR: redwood/console#xxxx)
- qa: simulation scenarios and validation scripts (PR: redwood/tests#xxxx)
